candidateRevisionStatus: Unpublished integration checkpoint; executable/input hashes identify the exact measured artifacts independently of final publication history.

method.order: S3 hello 30 s, C3 hello 30 s, C6 hello 30 s, Pocket Tank 30 s, then a separate S3 hello 300 s batch. Each case is main,candidate,main,candidate,main,candidate.
method.metric: POSIX time -p user seconds; ratio of candidate median to baseline median minus one. Positive means more user CPU time.
method.timer: Bash builtin time -p, invoked symmetrically for both arms because /usr/bin/time is unavailable.
method.quietWindow: Builds, tests, other emulator probes, compression, packaging and large unrelated hashes were stopped during timing. Concurrent task activity was limited to small document/JSON operations.
method.normalInputHashChecks: Each executable checked before and after every one of its runs; all firmware/ROM inputs checked at each batch end. Both executable hashes and every input were checked again after run 30.
method.exactness: Every sample compared with the first baseline in its case: full stdout SHA/bytes, stop reason, per-core/total instructions, exact guest seconds/cycles, exceptions and total IRQs. Curation additionally compared every source-IRQ report line across all six samples.

environment.measurementConditions: Caller declared exclusive quiet window. No affinity pinning, governor/frequency/thermal control, or hidden warmup. Three sequential main/candidate pairs per case. No new model/runtime source changes during measurement.

limitations: Only three pairs per case; no statistical confidence interval or zero-overhead claim.
Ranges overlap in every case. The C3 +0.9074 percent median increase is retained, not dismissed as proven noise.
Thirty-second S3 samples are below one host CPU second and use a timer reporting hundredths; the separate 300-second workload does not replace them.
Fixed main-then-candidate order, no hidden warmup, no CPU affinity pinning, and no frequency/thermal control. Quiet task activity does not isolate host scheduling or neighboring workloads.
Pocket Tank times decrease across rounds in both arms; all first samples remain included. No isolated improvement is attributed to a particular adaptation.
Native release CPU results on these fixtures are not browser/WASM speed, hardware timing, or exhaustive performance coverage of newly supported products.
Historical candidate 84e13293 and its incomplete +18.64 percent short S3 result are different artifacts/windows; the final data do not prove the earlier increase was noise.
redactions: Raw console/stderr bodies and local executable/cache paths are omitted.
Full measured numbers, source-IRQ report values, input/output hashes, normalized arguments and original raw-receipt/log hashes are preserved.
No process inventory, login name, hostname, device identifier or session identifier is included.
